mirror_alignment.required_alignment: Canonical and mirrored agile work item contracts must remain identical, including definition_of_ready and definition_of_done criteria.

purpose: Define the minimum ready and done contract for work items in the Sales AaaS repository so implementation, review, verification, release, and rollback expectations are explicit before production-impacting changes land.

applies_to.behavioral_scope: This contract is process metadata only and does not change runtime application behavior or shared API contracts.

source_alignment: AGENTS.md repo expectations and Definition of Done

work_item_required_fields.description: Stable ticket, issue, mission node, or PR identifier.
Short statement of the intended outcome.
The user, business, reliability, security, or operating problem being solved.
Observable conditions that make the work complete.
Repository paths, services, contracts, schemas, jobs, or workflows expected to change.
Risk level, rationale, high-risk surfaces, compatibility impact, and release gate expectations.
Required reviewers based on affected surfaces and risk.
Narrow checks, broader checks, smoke checks, and required evidence before merge or release.
Rollback action, constraints, data/schema posture, owner, and post-rollback verification.
Commands, test results, review evidence, deploy evidence, smoke evidence, and known gaps.

criteria: The requested outcome is specific enough to implement without guessing at product, legal, billing, security, or migration intent.
The affected repository paths and runtime surfaces are named, including whether the change targets demo-storage behavior, Postgres-backed behavior, or both.
Shared contract, public API, billing, auth, tenancy, audit, rate-limit, approval, provider webhook, and schema impacts are explicitly marked as impacted or not impacted.
The work is small enough for a branch and pull request, or has been decomposed into child work items with non-overlapping ownership.
Acceptance checks are measurable and include JSON/schema parsing when the deliverable is a machine-readable contract.
The validation plan starts with the narrowest meaningful checks and names when to run typecheck, tests, build, core verification, and smoke checks.
The rollback plan names the concrete rollback action, rollback owner, data compatibility constraints, and post-rollback validation.
Required owner and reviewer expectations are identified before implementation begins.
New production dependencies, public contract changes, plan key or billing behavior changes, migration semantics, or weakened safety controls are called out for explicit approval before editing.
Any product claim introduced or changed has an implementation evidence path or is gated, hidden, or downgraded.
Implementation is limited to the approved scope or documented scope expansion.
Runtime behavior, shared contracts, migrations, billing, auth, tenancy, audit, provider webhooks, and approval gates are preserved unless the work item explicitly requires a reviewed change.
Behavior-changing work has focused tests or a documented reason tests are not applicable.
Machine-readable artifacts parse successfully and any mirrored copies are kept aligned.
The narrowest meaningful validation passed before broader validation was run.
Required repo checks for the risk level have passed or are explicitly documented as blocked with the blocker and next safe step.
Pull request evidence includes changed files, risk classification, validation results, rollout notes, rollback action, and unresolved risks.
High-risk changes document backward compatibility, migration risk, provider or webhook failure modes, and rollback path.
Public-facing copy remains honest about beta scope and implemented capabilities.
Final handoff states what changed, what was verified, and what remains risky or unverified.
Documentation, metadata, tests, or isolated non-runtime configuration only.
No production dependency, public API, data model, billing, auth, tenancy, audit, webhook, or deployment behavior change.
minimum_validation: Parse or syntax check for changed machine-readable files
Targeted repository audit or relevant focused check

criteria: Application, workflow, or shared package behavior changes with bounded blast radius.
No irreversible data migration or safety-control weakening.
Auth, billing, tenancy, audit events, rate limits, approval-gated automation, provider webhooks, data model, migrations, or production deployment workflows are affected.
minimum_validation: Deployment or smoke validation in the target environment where credentials permit

criteria: Change may affect customer data integrity, tenant isolation, payment correctness, legal/compliance posture, or broad availability.
minimum_validation: Rollback rehearsal or documented rollback target confirmation

risk_classification.escalation_rule: Use the highest level that matches any affected surface.

ready_evidence: Problem, success conditions, affected surfaces, owner, reviewers, validation plan, and rollback plan are present.
Risk classification includes rationale and impacted high-risk surfaces.
Scope is compatible with a branch and pull request, or child work items have non-overlapping ownership.
done_evidence: Git branch and PR or PR-ready diff reference.
Exact commands or checks run and their result.
JSON parse, schema, typecheck, test, build, and smoke evidence as applicable.
Known blocked checks with blocker and next safe step.
Release notes for customer-visible or operational changes.
blocked_evidence: Whether the blocker is environmental, dependency-related, credential-related, or caused by the change.

owner: Keeps the diff scoped to the work item.
Updates or adds focused tests for behavior changes.
Runs and records the agreed validation plan.
Documents rollout, rollback, residual risk, and any intentionally deferred work.
reviewers: Verify the acceptance checks and evidence match the changed surface.
Review tenant isolation, organization/workspace correctness, billing correctness, webhook idempotency, audit coverage, approval gates, secrets, and public claims when touched.
Require explicit approval for new production dependencies, public contract changes, billing plan changes, migration semantics, or weakened safety controls.
Confirm rollback posture is credible before merge for production-impacting work.

required_specialist_reviews.review_focus: Session boundaries, organization/workspace correctness, access control, audit events, and rollback behavior.
Plan catalog alignment, checkout behavior, portal behavior, webhook idempotency, entitlement impact, and revenue risk.
Backward compatibility, forward-only posture, migration ordering, data repair path, and rollback constraints.
Signature verification, replay handling, idempotency, provider outage modes, and placeholder key safety.
Launch truthfulness, beta scope, implemented capability evidence, accessibility, and failure states.

narrow_first: Compare mirrored contract files when both exist.
when_to_skip_or_block: Only mark a check blocked when a required service, credential, dependency, or environment prerequisite is unavailable.
Record the exact blocker and next safe step rather than treating an unrun check as passed.

rollback_expectations.default_release_rollback_action: Redeploy the last known-good Cloudflare worker versions for web, api, and workflows, then rerun npm run smoke:cloudflare.
rollback_expectations.metadata_only_rollback_action: Revert the contract-file commit or close the PR without merge; no runtime service rollback is required.
rollback_expectations.schema_or_data_change_rule: Prefer forward-compatible migrations and behavior rollback. Only attempt database rollback when the migration has an explicitly safe rollback path.
post_rollback_validation: Run the same smoke or health checks that detected the release regression.
Document any customer-visible impact, data repair need, or follow-up prevention item.

must_include: Commands run with pass, fail, or blocked status.
Deploy or smoke evidence for release-impacting changes.
Rollback action for the current release path.
pull_request_expectations.merge_rule: Do not merge until required checks for the risk level are green or the exception is explicitly approved with documented residual risk.

non_goals: This file does not define application schemas, API contracts, billing plan keys, or runtime feature flags.
This file does not replace AGENTS.md, CI workflows, production-readiness reviews, or deploy rollback policy documents.
This file does not authorize bypassing branch, PR, review, verification, or release gates.
